Digital technologies, including AI and Digital Public Infrastructure, are becoming central to sustainable development. They can strengthen energy systems, improve public services and build resilience, but their rapid growth is also increasing demand for electricity, water, critical minerals and computing capacity.
 
As we approach 2030, this tension deserves greater attention. Around US$7 trillion could be invested in data centres and computing infrastructure, including more than US$5 trillion linked to AI. Yet developing economies may capture only around 10 per cent of AI’s projected US$15.7 trillion in global value.
 
The challenge is to ensure the digital transition advances sustainable development without adding new environmental pressures or widening inequality.
 
On Thursday, 16 July, I will be speaking at the High-level Political Forum side event, Advancing Digital Environmental Sustainability for SDG Implementation: Aligning the Global Digital Compact with the HLPF, at UN Headquarters in New York.
 
I will also be sharing insights from UNDP’s latest publication, The Energy Sprint of the AI Race, which explores how countries can align AI, energy, infrastructure, skills and natural resources to capture the opportunities of the digital transition.
 
We will discuss how AI, Digital Public Infrastructure and other innovations can accelerate the SDGs while managing their environmental footprint, and how the Global Digital Compact can support a more sustainable Beyond 2030 agenda.
 
Digital transformation and sustainable development must move together so that technology creates jobs, strengthens resilience and improves lives.
 
📅Date: Thursday, 16 July 2026
🕐Time: 13:15–14:30 ET
📍Venue: UN Headquarters, Conference Room 4, New York
